facts.text: The movie's Georgia quarry opening is credited to a real quarry: the Ferrante Bros. Quarry in Bernardsville, New Jersey, listed among the film's shooting locations.
Drive-In Totals: Twenty nine dead bodies. Two fist fights. One motor vehicle chase. One brawl. Ground-seepage goo tasting. And Drive-In Academy Awards for Michael Moriarty and Paul Sorvino.
Director Larry Cohen stretched a budget of about $1.7 million into this movie. In 1983 the Hollywood Reporter had listed it, as "Stuff!", with a $10 million budget.
Director Larry Cohen encouraged star Michael Moriarty to improvise, and Moriarty's jazzy, ad-libbed one-liners became the film's signature. Cohen likened his method to jazz: change things as you go.
Jason and his bullying older brother are played by real-life brothers Scott and Brian Bloom. Brian later played Pike in the 2010 film version of The A-Team.
The day The Stuff opened in New York, a hurricane hit and newspapers weren't delivered. Director Larry Cohen says nobody got to read the great reviews.
Clara Peller, famous for Wendy's 1984 "Where's the Beef?" ads, appears in a parody commercial in this film asking "Where's the Stuff?"
Monologuist and actor Eric Bogosian (Talk Radio) has an uncredited bit part as one of the grocery clerks.
An unseasonable blizzard hit the location shoot, so director Larry Cohen simply wrote the snow into the movie. The lights weren't built for snow and exploded, though nobody was hurt.
Director Larry Cohen said he got the idea from endless product recalls in the news and our daily junk food habit: an imaginary dessert that millions gobble up while it harms them.
Drive-In Totals: One rabid junkie dog. Bureaucrat devoured by a canine.
Georgia is played by New York's Hudson Valley, between Kingston and New Paltz. Every license plate you see in the movie is from New York State.
Garrett Morris' 'Chocolate Chip' Charlie is modeled on Wally 'Famous' Amos, who built a chocolate chip cookie empire.
Director Larry Cohen wanted rising star Arsenio Hall as Chocolate Chip Charlie. New World Pictures wanted someone better known and cast SNL original Garrett Morris.
Asked about working with Larry Cohen in an A.V. Club interview, Garrett Morris said if you have nothing nice to say, say nothing, and added nothing more.
The in-movie Stuff commercials are stuffed with cameos: Abe Vigoda (The Godfather, Barney Miller), Brooke Adams, Laurene Landon, Tammy Grimes and Jason Evers all pitch the dessert.
The FBI contact Moriarty's character names, Special Agent Frank Herbert, shares a name with the author of the sci-fi novel Dune.
For some chase scenes, director Larry Cohen used foam made from blended fish bones. It stank so badly the actors ran to a river to wash after shooting.
The Nightline segment about missing families uses real footage of ABC's news show Nightline, which is credited as a feature in the film.
Star Michael Moriarty once stopped a 1971 Houston stage performance mid-show, told the audience he was too tired, and walked off. He's also a jazz pianist.
Director Larry Cohen was a guerrilla filmmaker: he reportedly slipped money to security guards to shoot in places like New York's Chrysler Building.
Besides upstate New York, the shoot used the Riverdale neighborhood of the Bronx, a cement factory in Cementon, the town of Accord, and a few days in New Jersey.
Drive-In Totals: Shaving cream fu. Kung fu. One sucker punch. Food tossing. Gratuitous bikini models. Infected attack bed.
Stand-ins for the Stuff included Häagen-Dazs ice cream, yogurt, Tofutti and whipped cream, plus fire-extinguisher foam for the giant wave that bursts through a wall.
Future Oscar winner Mira Sorvino debuts as a factory worker. She was visiting her father, star Paul Sorvino (Colonel Spears), on set, so he and director Larry Cohen stuck her in front of the camera.
The Stuff turns up as a movie playing at the Starcourt Mall in Stranger Things season 3, another story about compulsive consumption turning people into mindless zombies.
The motel room where the Stuff attacks was built to rotate upside down. Director Larry Cohen says it's the same room used in A Nightmare on Elm Street for Johnny Depp's bed scene.
For the motel scene, director Larry Cohen borrowed the rotating-room trick from the Fred Astaire musical Royal Wedding. Crew clung to the outside of the set to spin it upside down.
Director Larry Cohen's first cut ran about 30 minutes longer. New World Pictures wanted it faster, so he cut commercials and a romance scene. That long cut resurfaced on Arrow's 2025 release.
Director Larry Cohen says New World Pictures wanted a gory horror film and got a satire. He feels selling it as horror hurt it, and it flopped on release.
Director Larry Cohen said the film takes cigarettes and alcohol to an extreme, noting tobacco companies probably killed more people than all the wars combined.
The Stuff is one of Harry Potter star Rupert Grint's favorite films.
On VHS, rental stores got a promo of an inflatable tub of the Stuff with the creature oozing out, made to hang from the ceiling.
Colonel Spears' castle headquarters is the gatehouse of the Mohonk Mountain House in New Paltz, New York.
Michael Moriarty and Paul Sorvino (Colonel Spears) later reunited for 31 Law & Order episodes as prosecutor Ben Stone and Sergeant Phil Cerreta. Sorvino's daughter Mira made her debut here.
After flopping in about 30 theaters, The Stuff found its audience on video, where its gross, misleading cover art lured in plenty of 1980s splatter fans.
Drive-In Totals: Exploding heads. Exploding bodies. Multiple exploding buildings. Exploding Garrett Morris. Goo burning. A worker sliced in half by an eighteen-wheeler. Organized child abuse.
The film's exploding-factory effects led to a lawsuit. Director Larry Cohen paid half the price, and Effects Associates v. Cohen became a landmark US copyright case on written transfers.
Director Larry Cohen's wife Cynthia Costas Cohen is a psychotherapist and sculptor, while Cohen dictated his scripts into a hand-held tape recorder rather than typing.
Eight tons of firefighting foam were used for one sequence. Per director Larry Cohen's team, the foam was made partly from fish bones, which gave it a fetid smell.
The radio station is said to be near Atlanta, but its signs read WGHQ and the exterior is WBPM, both in Kingston, New York.
Director Larry Cohen's longer 118-minute first cut was reportedly one he was begrudgingly forced to trim and rescore for New World Pictures.
Four models of Garrett Morris' head were built for Charlie's transformation. Director Larry Cohen has claimed he still owns one.
The Stuff's consumerism-as-horror satire predates John Carpenter's They Live by three years.
Germany cut about 10 seconds for violence to get an 18 rating. In 2016 the cut was waived and the uncut film received a 16 rating.
The executives' office, stuffed polar bear included, looks uncannily like Mr. Burns' office in The Simpsons, which later referenced the film.
Listen for a car horn between the executive's lines "We tested it. We tested it in a small Illinois town." It's a stray street noise left in.
Drive-In Totals: Two and a half stars. Joe Bob says check it out.
